case_title: Sunil Dutt Sharma v. State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi)
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of s.302, convicted of s.304-B
neutral_facts: The accused, a man, was tried for causing the death of his wife, which occurred within two years of their marriage. There was a demand for dowry and evidence of cruelty or harassment. The autopsy report showed external injuries, but the cause of death was attributed to asphyxia from strangulation. The trial court acquitted the accused of the more severe charge of murder due to lack of direct involvement in the strangulation, but found him guilty of the lesser charge of dowry death. The trial court's findings indicated that some injuries were attributable to the accused, though not fatal. The accused had no prior criminal record and was about 21 years old at the time of the incident. The High Court affirmed the conviction and sentence.
